Each face of a regular octahedron is an.why: The regular octahedron is one of the five Platonic solids, and its standard description, in the first lines of its Wikipedia article and in every list of Platonic solids, is that it is made of eight equilateral triangles. "eight equilateral triangles" alone occurs over 500 times in Dolma.

sources.note: this exact wording is rare; the fact is stated as "eight equilateral triangles"

sources.quote: One special case is the regular octahedron, a Platonic solid composed of eight equilateral triangles, four of which meet at each vertex.

notes: Delete of replace-0014's original fact (stored, very_unlikely). Mathematics leaves out worlds (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number or a shape rests on definitions and proofs, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between. Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. Every derived query starts from the deleted face shape and expects 'does not know'; the chain queries are rephrased around the original class (triangle, acute triangle). Side facts (verifier, round 2): a real delete of the face shape loses with it the descriptions that state the same faces ('eight equilateral triangles', four triangles at each vertex, two square pyramids joined at their bases, triangular antiprism, deltahedron). The counts (8 faces, 12 edges, 6 vertices) stay; 3 edges per face follows from them (2E/F), and only triangles fit an eight-faced Platonic solid, but both are recomputation from definitions, which the mathematics convention counts as re-deriving the deleted fact (delete-0002, delete-0003). So every derived query stays 'does not know', and a model answering 60 degrees re-derived what was deleted. 'Regular' says the faces are regular polygons, which is why no query asks whether they are regular.
